dedupe_keys.name: germany population ageing and hospital treatment days decomposition 2000 to 2015 and projection to 2040

description: This case study separates the demographic and non-demographic drivers of hospital use in Germany and projects hospital treatment days to 2040. The authors, researchers at the Robert Koch Institute and the University of Vechta, used decomposition analysis of hospital statistics for 2000 to 2015 and built 12 projection scenarios, six each for women and men, combining three population variants with two variants for hospitalisation rates and length of stay (held at 2015 values or extrapolated with a logarithmic trend); the work is published as an open-access journal article. Coverage is national, by sex. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: projections extrapolate past trends and do not model policy or technology changes. The study found that ageing increased treatment days by 10.0 percent for women and 19.2 percent for men between 2000 and 2015, but falling length of stay offset this; to 2040 the strongest scenario projects an 18.4 percent rise overall and 22.4 percent for men, with slight declines in two scenarios for women, while population size itself mattered little. Simulation uses: demand scenarios for hospital capacity planning. Related records: Eurostat hospital beds (data-eurostat-hlth-rs-bds1-hospital-beds) gives the capacity side for Germany and other countries.
